summary: Correct Phase 6 guidance and machine contracts after staged-code review; cover follow-up peer, Controller transport and UI retry changes.

guide.reason: The prior pages overstated Core-local UI and automatic recover-original behavior, gave unsafe retry guidance, and had verification sections predating later lab reports. The guide index now reflects running BIOS crash-consistent capture, and the Controller test-restore flow documents operator inspection, recorded result and per-VM confirmed cleanup. Master-side signed-authority capacity refusal and operator retry guidance are now documented. Test restore guidance now distinguishes native provenance proof for passed/failed recording and refusal after a VM ID is reused. Exact original-Core allocating-stage restore resume is now explained without implying promoted-master replay. Legacy allocating restore recovery now requires immutable point and complete native artifact proof. A successful test VM keeps its point pin until cleanup, including member work and promoted-master pending cleanup recovery. A bounded disposable member BIOS test restore now verifies the operator-recorded Failed path and typed-ID cleanup; Passed and interrupted paths remain open. Replace verification now distinguishes the bounded native UEFI/vTPM restore-as-new evidence from still-open native replace cutover. Restore guidance now explains catalog/payload mismatch and old-member refusal before new native effects. UI retry lifecycle correction changes no operator step; existing guidance to reconcile uncertain tasks remains applicable.

api.reason: Documents backup-v1 capability acknowledgement, Controller target-host routing, authenticated member backup/test-cleanup GET/POST, signed paged backup-authority transfer including page lengths and durable metadata receipts, and Core-local metadata replay Result unions. Pool transfer status now includes a durable catalog-rebuild stage after promotion commit and before member repointing. The authenticated Core peer VM route adds release-restore-placement with exact owner provenance and native absence precondition; the Controller client contract is unchanged. Local restore/repository descriptions track Core-derived NFS mounts and NVRAM/vTPM restoration. Restore pins in the signed Core authority remain the existing array shape but now permit several pins for one point and require unique operation IDs. Planned pool transfer now refuses pending backup work before freeze; fenced promotion projects inherited pending backup results as needs_attention without replay. Core-local exact restore retry returns retained outcome after promotion without adding a route. Existing Core backup routes can now refuse metadata writes before acceptance at the 64 MiB signed-authority capacity boundary; response fields and endpoint shapes are unchanged. Core peer adds authenticated read-only POST /api/v1/pool/backup/verify-test for exact member native creator/current proof; Controller verify and cleanup request shapes remain unchanged, but Core may refuse unproved current VMs. Existing restore operation and result contracts now permit internal exact allocating-stage reconciliation on the executing Core; no endpoint or field changed. Exact allocating-stage retry also binds new native journals to the manifest digest and disk descriptors; older journals fail closed unless full artifacts are proven. This is internal Core recovery under the existing operation contract. Existing Core cleanup/operation contracts now rehydrate only exact inherited pending receipts and preserve test pins through owner deletion; no new request field or route. Rehydrated promotion cleanup journals are internal/PeerDispatched and do not claim the former master's Controller result ownership. The existing authenticated agent-report Result contract now lets a later same-host terminal backup Result settle an earlier Controller needs_attention row; no request or response field changes. Core continues explicit Controller-owned backup outcomes after Result ACK and Controller may settle only the matching own nonterminal operation from that outcome; native same-ID VM-create and peer work are excluded. Outcome catch-up covers backup metadata commands and Controller ownership lookup binds both host and kind for colliding IDs. The existing authenticated member backup peer reply now retries exact terminal-run/journal status lag while rejecting changed pool, host, intent and target; no schema or client route changed. Restore reservations now pin the master catalog manifest digest in BackupRun; the new authenticated member POST /api/v1/pool/backup/restore requires catalog_point and GET /api/v1/pool/backup/{operation_id} returns durable catalog_manifest_sha256 for exact retry. Older members and legacy unbound restore runs fail closed; the Controller client routes are unchanged. UI #45–47 retry audit uses existing client and Controller/Core contracts; it changes no route, payload or schema.

roadmap.reason: Current website milestone status returns to testing while preserving the dated 2026-09-27 disposable close as historical evidence; later staged code and acceptance reruns remain open.

state.record: The pool master retains repositories, policies, runs, catalog, restore pins and metadata mutation receipts in its Core backup stores. Its pool-vms.json owner record also holds create_operation_id for exact failed-restore placement release; signed authority transfer carries that record. The signed backup_manifest references digest-checked pages for promotion. The peer record holds the active backup root and durable promotion catalog-rebuild stage. A fresh Controller adopts the master-reported backup and VM inventories through authenticated protocol-v2 reports after backup-v1 acknowledgement. Member execution uses its durable agent command journal. pool-backup-pins.json holds one pin per operation; legacy point-keyed entries are reindexed on read without releasing unresolved protection. New restore BackupRun entries also retain the selected master catalog manifest_sha256, carried through signed authority pages and member durable runs for exact reconciliation.
state.reason: Peer dispatch, capability gating, retries and the corrected Run owner gate change how Core-owned backup records are transported and projected, not who owns them. Creator provenance for safe restore placement release stays in the pool master's VM owner record.
